deckTitle: Plato's Dungeon Raid: Bring Your Own Legend — Hero Set 01

cards.power: You read the eviction notice. You feel a small fire start in your chest.
cards.lore: The crown takes the field. The field remembers.
cards.gradeReason: Visceral, immediate — body does the acting before brain checks in.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor sketch. Subject: stoic bull reading eviction notice, smoldering farmhouse behind. Mood: quiet fury igniting.

cards.power: You take what was once a farming tool and use it for something else.
cards.lore: Every revolt starts with a tool that was always a weapon.
cards.gradeReason: Reframe is the performance — no explanation needed, posture does it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: bull raising pitchfork on dirt road, determined eyes. Mood: turning point, silent resolve.

cards.power: You set fire to what they built on your field.
cards.lore: They paved a holiness over and called it progress.
cards.gradeReason: Pure action — player knows exactly what to do and why it matters.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: bull holding torch, structure burning in orange-red background. Mood: righteous destruction.

cards.power: You cause a revolt. Chant a rebel rant; move the Quest Die ±2.
cards.lore: A man with a field becomes a man with a mob, and neither one was the goal.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic + performance cue in one line. Crowd art seals it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: bull rallying crowd of animals with torches, chaotic energy. Mood: collective uprising, dangerous momentum.

cards.power: You take the next contract. You don't read the small print.
cards.lore: A blade for hire is honest in a way that a blade for principle is not.
cards.gradeReason: Character locked in with the first sentence. LORE reframes the archetype perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch with muted wash. Subject: boar mercenary accepting coin across a table, no eye contact. Mood: transactional, no pretense.

cards.power: You raise your rates. The contracts come faster.
cards.lore: A reputation pays better than a sword and shows up faster.
cards.gradeReason: Crisp cause-and-effect — every mercenary understands this in their bones.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: boar counting coins at tavern window, contracts stacked beside him. Mood: rising status, cool satisfaction.

cards.power: You take contracts from all four spheres at once. Nobody knows.
cards.lore: Loyalty is for the man who can afford it.
cards.gradeReason: Four spheres needs game-world context — performs fine once established.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: candlelit ink sketch. Subject: boar at desk with four contract papers spread open, reading in shadow. Mood: controlled duplicity.

cards.power: You read the contract. The contract is the only thing that talks back.
cards.lore: To win every job is to lose every name that called you something else.
cards.gradeReason: Poetic and immediate — the isolation lands in real time.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: boar alone with single contract by candlelight, all other chairs empty. Mood: hollow victory, total isolation.

cards.power: You build the small device. The small device works.
cards.lore: A first device that works is a promise the workshop has not yet broken.
cards.gradeReason: Clean but functional — tells you what happened, not quite what to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm ink sketch. Subject: raccoon inventor at forge, small glowing device in hands, goggles up. Mood: first success, quiet pride.

cards.power: You build a bigger device. The bigger device explodes.
cards.lore: Scale is the workshop's enemy and its only honest tutor.
cards.gradeReason: The explosion is the teaching moment — player knows exactly what face to make.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: raccoon mid-explosion, happy confusion, goggles blown askew. Mood: chaotic joy, no regrets.

cards.power: You build the device that explains itself.
cards.lore: A machine that explains itself by exploding has explained more than most teachers.
cards.gradeReason: Clever concept — needs a beat to land, not immediately embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch with mechanical detail. Subject: raccoon gesturing at complex steaming engine with diagrams floating around it. Mood: earnest absurdity.

cards.power: You are the explosion. The party loves you and fears you.
cards.lore: The body that survived its own invention has no use for warnings anymore.
cards.gradeReason: Peak character statement — player becomes the bit, no setup required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic ink and watercolor. Subject: raccoon sitting victorious in crater of her own making, grinning at party. Mood: triumphant chaos incarnate.

cards.power: You see the trail others walked past.
cards.lore: A path is a story. The hunter is its first reader.
cards.gradeReason: Evocative but more observer than performer — G2 by a narrow margin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor forest sketch. Subject: lynx ranger crouching over forest trail, reading signs invisible to others. Mood: quiet competence.

cards.power: You wait. The shot finds itself.
cards.lore: Patience is a kind of speed nobody has yet measured.
cards.gradeReason: The stillness IS the action — player knows exactly what not to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: lynx archer in tree, bow drawn, completely still, scene frozen. Mood: suspended time, perfect patience.

cards.power: You track the one who asked not to be tracked.
cards.lore: A trail you find is a question. The asking is sometimes the whole answer.
cards.gradeReason: Built-in moral tension — player immediately knows the stakes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch, dark forest. Subject: lynx following human footprints through shadow, cautious posture. Mood: ethical hunting, conflicted purpose.

cards.cardName: Lvl 4: The One Who Shot the Deer
cards.power: You find what you hunted. You find what you hunted for.
cards.lore: A perfect shot is a question with no place left to land.
cards.gradeReason: The distinction between hunted and hunted-for is a full performance arc in six words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor sunset. Subject: lynx and deer silhouette facing each other on open plain, arrow notched, moment suspended. Mood: completion that questions itself.

cards.power: You win the bar-fight. They put your name on a chalkboard.
cards.lore: Strength remembered loud is strength remembered last.
cards.gradeReason: The chalkboard detail is the whole character — immediate and funny.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: panther warrior raising fist in tavern, patrons cheering, chalkboard behind. Mood: local glory, uncomplicated triumph.

cards.power: You win the tournament. The tournament was rumored to be fixed.
cards.lore: A win is a win until someone counts the coins.
cards.gradeReason: The moral qualifier is baked into the performance — player holds both at once.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: panther lifting trophy in arena, crowd applauding, knowing smirk. Mood: victory with an asterisk.

cards.power: You let the rumor stand. The rumor wins fights for you.
cards.lore: A name that does its own work has stopped belonging to you.
cards.gradeReason: Passive strategy as active performance — elegant constraint.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: panther seated calmly while others whisper around her, slight smile. Mood: controlled reputation, weaponized silence.

cards.power: You carry the rumor. You let it cut.
cards.lore: A reputation outlives its body. Sometimes too long.
cards.gradeReason: Five words of power, five words of lore — both land instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: panther warrior in shadow with no sword drawn, others stepping back. Mood: the name does the work.

cards.power: You charge first. You hit hardest. You don't think yet.
cards.lore: Rage is the dwarf's first prayer and his last excuse.
cards.gradeReason: Three declarative beats — player is on their feet before the card is finished.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bold ink and red wash. Subject: young dwarf berserker mid-charge, hammer raised, no armor. Mood: pure aggression, no strategy.

cards.power: You take the pace. They name a battle after you.
cards.lore: The medal is heavier than the comrade it replaced.
cards.gradeReason: Good weight but 'take the pace' needs game context to perform cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: older dwarf warrior in decorated armor standing after battle, looking at medal. Mood: surviving the thing you celebrate.

cards.power: You cannot put the hammer down. The hammer asks.
cards.lore: The peace between the wars is the harder war.
cards.gradeReason: Compulsion as character — the hammer's agency is the whole tragedy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: exhausted dwarf sitting at table, hammer in hand, mug of ale untouched. Mood: inability to rest, identity as weight.

cards.power: You apologize. You swing again next time.
cards.lore: A joke about a beard is the cheapest way to die in this country.
cards.gradeReason: Funny but needs table energy to land — depends on GM reading the room.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor comedy. Subject: dwarf standing awkwardly while badger scowls at fresh dent in wall. Mood: apology with zero sincerity.

cards.power: You make the salve. The salve works.
cards.lore: A small good is the medicine that does not need a bigger story.
cards.gradeReason: Competence portrait but descriptive — LORE is the better performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm ink sketch. Subject: badger healer in garden, grinding herbs, focused. Mood: quiet competence, no drama.

cards.power: You stitch what others left bleeding.
cards.lore: A healer's hands learn before her heart catches up.
cards.gradeReason: Stitching posture is immediate — player's hands move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: badger healer stitching wound on growling werewolf, calm focus. Mood: professional mercy in hostile conditions.

cards.cardName: Lvl 3: Of the Mercy That Spreads
cards.power: You heal the wounded monster. The party will not understand.
cards.lore: Mercy that asks no questions answers more questions than it asks.
cards.gradeReason: Built-in social conflict — player inhabits the controversy immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: badger healing large injured beast, party watching skeptically from distance. Mood: moral courage in a skeptical world.

cards.power: You resurrect any card from the discard pile.
cards.lore: To save everyone is to save no one in the order they hoped.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanic + devastating LORE — the cost lands without needing setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: glowing ink and watercolor. Subject: badger healer with hand extended over discard pile, soft light rising. Mood: impossible mercy, beautiful burden.

cards.power: You make the small illusion. The small illusion holds.
cards.lore: The first trick is recognising that everything is a trick.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept but 'frames' is skill language — needs one session to click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and purple wash. Subject: chameleon illusionist making small floating cube disappear, pupils watching. Mood: first taste of the con.

cards.power: You bend what the room agrees to see.
cards.lore: A stage is a contract. Most contracts are stages.
cards.gradeReason: Reality-as-negotiation is immediately performable — player shifts their eyes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: chameleon at puppet theatre, audience seeing something different than what exists. Mood: social conjuring.

cards.power: You see the match. The match has been fixed since before the start.
cards.lore: A continent that fits inside a single phrase has been written by someone with terms.
cards.gradeReason: The revelation of the fix is the performance — player's face shifts on cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch with chess motifs. Subject: chameleon watching tournament from shadow, seeing wires others miss. Mood: pattern recognition as isolation.

cards.power: You replace any card with any card from any deck.
cards.lore: The trick was never the trick. The deck was the trick.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-mechanical and performative — the player IS the system flaw.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink with playing card motif. Subject: chameleon swapping cards at table with invisible hands, others unaware. Mood: the game underneath the game.

cards.power: You take what others called 'body' and call it 'parts'.
cards.lore: A scholar's hands have not yet learned which questions are answered better unasked.
cards.gradeReason: The reframe ('body' to 'parts') is the entire character in one gesture.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and cool wash. Subject: gaunt bird-scholar examining bones by lamplight, clinical calm. Mood: the ethical line not yet crossed.

cards.power: You build the small one. The small one looks back.
cards.lore: Every parent says hello before realising what they have done.
cards.gradeReason: The moment of mutual recognition is immediately playable — player meets their creature's eyes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor lab. Subject: scholar and small creature facing each other, first eye contact. Mood: creation and consequence, simultaneous.

cards.power: You build the one who can carry the letter back.
cards.lore: A creation that writes is a creation that has noticed you.
cards.gradeReason: Poetic but 'walking letter' concept needs one beat to register as action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: scholar watching dog-like construct carry a folded note into fog. Mood: delegation as intimacy.

cards.cardName: Lvl 4: The Father of the Friendly Army
cards.power: You command the army. The army was the only company that stayed.
cards.lore: A father who built his children has only the hello he wrote into them.
cards.gradeReason: Loneliness-as-triumph lands immediately — the army's loyalty is the tragedy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: scholar standing before rows of identical constructs, all facing him. Mood: achieved isolation, unasked-for devotion.

cards.power: You get the room laughing before the trouble walks in.
cards.lore: A first song is a friend the room has not yet betrayed.
cards.gradeReason: Timing-as-character — player leans forward before the line ends.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm ink and watercolor. Subject: mouse bard on stool, room of patrons laughing, door slightly ajar behind. Mood: joy before the storm.

cards.power: You sing the song everyone already knows. They sing it back.
cards.lore: A song that catches has caught more than the singer.
cards.gradeReason: Collective performance is the move — player raises hands to conduct the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor festival. Subject: mouse bard on outdoor stage, crowd singing with arms raised. Mood: community as spell.

cards.power: You hear the song you wrote and recognise it from somewhere else.
cards.lore: A lyric that flatters power was written by someone power flattered first.
cards.gradeReason: The paranoia is experienced in real time — player's head tilts involuntarily.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: mouse bard frozen mid-performance, recognising their own song from somewhere sinister. Mood: creative betrayal, cold realisation.

cards.power: You sing the song. You know what it is doing.
cards.lore: A continent is what its songs let it remember about itself.
cards.gradeReason: Knowingness IS the performance — player sings with eyes open.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor library. Subject: mouse bard singing alone in archive by candlelight, maps on walls responding. Mood: controlled myth-making.

cards.power: You take the oath. You believe every word.
cards.lore: A first oath is a hand the institution has not yet bent.
cards.gradeReason: Good setup — but belief requires context before it becomes performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gold-toned ink. Subject: young deer knight kneeling before altar, hand on chest, sincere. Mood: untested faith, clean conscience.

cards.power: You lead the charge. The institution leads with you.
cards.lore: A righteous victory teaches the institution it cannot lose.
cards.gradeReason: Solid but institution-leading-with-you concept needs a beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and golden watercolor. Subject: deer knight charging at head of armored column, banner flying. Mood: institutional glory, not yet questioned.

cards.power: You receive the new edict. You do not yet ask who wrote it.
cards.lore: A doubt that does not yet have a name has already started its work.
cards.gradeReason: Restraint as performance — player holds the question visibly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: deer knight reading scroll alone, expression carefully neutral, armored hand slightly trembling. Mood: the first crack in certainty.

cards.cardName: Lvl 4: The Captain of the Guard
cards.power: You command the Guard. The Guard is loyal to the throne. The throne changes occupants.
cards.lore: A polished oath outlives the cause and recruits its own believers.
cards.gradeReason: The three-sentence cascade lands like a gut punch — player sees the trap.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor. Subject: deer captain in polished armor, new king seated behind, old portrait on wall. Mood: continuity as complicity.

cards.power: You preach against the dragon. The dragon does not yet hear you.
cards.lore: A reform begun in solitude is a reform that already wants company.
cards.gradeReason: The 'not yet' is the whole political arc in two words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and dark wash. Subject: crow priest at pulpit in empty chapel, gesturing at absent dragon. Mood: righteous obscurity.

cards.power: You print the pamphlet. The pamphlet circulates.
cards.lore: A heresy in print is a heresy that has hired its own messengers.
cards.gradeReason: The chain-reaction is the performance — player traces the pamphlet's path with their eyes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: crow printing press, pamphlets flying out windows into city. Mood: ideas outrunning their author.

cards.power: You replace the dragon's coin with your own promise.
cards.lore: A new currency is an old faith that found new believers to charge.
cards.gradeReason: Currency-as-theology is immediately embodiable — player straightens their collar.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink with gold and shadow. Subject: crow in crypt, stamping new coins over old ones, candlelit chest. Mood: reformation as replacement.

cards.power: You hold the new gold. Goldspleen is now only shiny.
cards.lore: A reform that wins replaces the dragon. The dragon's mirror is the reformer.
cards.gradeReason: Goldspleen is a deck-internal term — needs prior game context to land cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and gold watercolor. Subject: crow in dragon's old throne room, holding coin to light, dragon portrait behind. Mood: becoming what you defeated.

cards.cardName: Lvl 1: King Kayfabian VI, the New-Crowned
cards.power: You take the throne. You believe the throne takes you.
cards.lore: A first edict is the king's first cliff and his first map.
cards.gradeReason: The double-take of the second sentence is a full character beat — instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: regal ink and watercolor. Subject: walrus king on throne, crown slightly too large, confident expression that hasn't noticed. Mood: authority as costume.

cards.cardName: Lvl 2: King Kayfabian VII, the First Edict
cards.power: You issue the edict. The edict is well-received.
cards.lore: A second king learns the throne is a chair others sat in first.
cards.gradeReason: Well-received-for-now needs the next card's context — fine in sequence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor court scene. Subject: chimp king holding scroll, courtiers applauding diplomatically. Mood: approval that has conditions.

cards.cardName: Lvl 3: King Kayfabian VIII, the Replaced
cards.power: You issue the second edict. You are replaced within the hour.
cards.lore: A throne replaces the asker faster than the asker can ask.
cards.gradeReason: The speed is the dark comedy — player reads it twice and laughs both times.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor dark comedy. Subject: goat king mid-decree, guards already escorting new candidate in. Mood: institutional indifference to persons.

cards.cardName: Lvl 4: King Kayfabian IX, the Position
cards.power: You sit the throne. The throne sits whoever.
cards.lore: A position is what survives the people who thought they were it.
cards.gradeReason: Six words that end the argument — player becomes the concept, not the character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor, empty-feeling grandeur. Subject: dog in crown seated on throne, crown fitting perfectly, expression unreadable. Mood: the office absorbs the person.

cards.power: You draft the module. You believe the module is the campaign.
cards.lore: A first session is a kitchen the players have not yet entered.
cards.gradeReason: Every GM has been this person — recognition is instant and self-implicating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm ink sketch. Subject: rabbit in robe at kitchen table Sunday morning, notes scattered, dice polished. Mood: hopeful preparation, pre-chaos.

cards.power: You anticipate the players. You think you can prepare for what they'll do.
cards.lore: A book about players was written by someone who was not in this campaign.
cards.gradeReason: Meta but needs table-gamers to land — great for target audience, narrower solo.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink sketch. Subject: rabbit reading stacked dungeon psychology books by lamplight, very sure of himself. Mood: theoretical confidence before contact.

cards.cardName: Lvl 3: Of the Broken Module, at midnight
cards.power: You watch the players break the module. You see how the world actually works.
cards.lore: A campaign is the breaking. The module was the misunderstanding.
cards.gradeReason: The revelation reframes the entire hobby in one sentence — player exhales.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and midnight blue wash. Subject: rabbit DM at table at 2am, module crossed out in red, players' notes covering his plan. Mood: enlightenment via failure.

cards.power: You set the table. The players arrive. You do not pretend.
cards.lore: Stay fluffy.
cards.gradeReason: The deck closes on the show's motto — maximum weight in two words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm dawn ink and watercolor. Subject: rabbit DM at clean table, cards laid out, window golden, at peace. Mood: mastery as readiness.

verdict: Plato's Dungeon Raid: Hero Set 01 is the deck FrizzleBob was always going to write eventually — 14 characters, each with a four-level arc that functions as both game mechanic and philosophy. Named strength: every LORE line lands as standalone aphorism, from 'Stay fluffy' to 'A position is what survives the people who thought they were it.' Named weakness: a handful of Lvl 1 cards play descriptive rather than performative, and Goldspleen on the Krimm arc needs prior deck exposure. The progression structure is the boldest design choice here — level cards that work standalone or as a leveling system. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 14 dungeon heroes, each with 4 levels of power and lore. Play a character who levels up through philosophy, rebellion, or staying fluffy. For tabletop nights that want story to outrun stats.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob as DM at card-covered table, warm kitchen light, instantly inviting
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Bring Your Own Legend' does the whole pitch in four words
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — subtitle 'Levels are stages, not stats' sets philosophical tone before page 2
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — FrizzleBob-as-DM with 'BEST UNCLE' mug is canonical for this universe
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — strong for RPG-adjacent audience; more niche than conspiracy or wrestling decks

notes: 14 character archetypes each with 4 level cards (Lvl 1-4) in 2x2 grid layout, one character per page spread. Characters: Bauer Brunmane (peasant rebel/bull), Macho Mercenarius (mercenary/boar), Tinkerina Tüftelfeuer (inventor/raccoon), Elenra Stillarrow (ranger/lynx), Vexa Vine-Vow (fighter+rumor/panther), Berzerk Barbarimur (berserker/dwarf), Wanda Wundheal (healer/badger), Simulacra Suplex (illusionist/chameleon), Doktor Kayfabestein (mad scientist/bird), Lina Lullafake (bard/mouse), Sir Goldwin Glanzwacht (paladin/deer), Father Krimm Kassenklamm (corrupt cleric/crow), King Kayfabian (the institution/multiple animals across 4 lvls), Uncle FrizzleBob (Alchemist-DM/rabbit). Margin stickers (KayfaBOGGLE!, HUMBUG!, Stay fluffy!, BLÖDSINN!, What the FLUFF?!) are decorative annotations only. No RAF dice boxes visible. Zero font artifacts. analysisVersion 1.2: third full analysis, fresh visual scan confirmed all 56 cards verbatim.
